title: Chemical Nomenclature
standard_code: Chemistry 1, Quarter 2: Compounds and Their Formulas
standard_text: Chemical nomenclature: naming and writing formulas of ionic compounds (including polyatomic ions and variable-charge metals), binary molecular compounds, acids and simple organic compounds. (summary of the Strengthened Senior High School curriculum, Chemistry 1, Quarter 2)
meta_desc: Free Chemistry 1 worksheets (Strengthened SHS curriculum, Quarter 2): ionic compounds, polyatomic ions, molecular compounds with prefixes, acids and simple organic names. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Molecular: use prefixes such as di- and tri-.
body_html:
How to think about it

Ionic compounds are named metal first, then the non-metal with -ide: NaCl is sodium chloride. Polyatomic ions keep their names (sulfate SO₄²⁻, nitrate NO₃⁻). Metals with more than one charge use Roman numerals: FeCl₃ is iron(III) chloride.

Binary molecular compounds use prefixes: CO₂ is carbon dioxide, N₂O₄ is dinitrogen tetroxide. Acids: HCl(aq) is hydrochloric acid, H₂SO₄ is sulfuric acid. Simple organic compounds are named from the number of carbons: methane, ethane, propane.

Example

Name CuO.

Copper is Cu²⁺ here

Answer: copper(II) oxide

Example

Formula of dinitrogen pentoxide?

di = 2, penta = 5

Answer: N₂O₅

Common mistakes

  • Using prefixes for ionic compounds.
  • Forgetting Roman numerals for transition metals.
  • Writing the charges in the formula.

faq.a: It can form Fe²⁺ or Fe³⁺, so the name must show which.

items.q: What is the formula of strontium iodide?
items.e: Strontium forms Sr<sup>2+</sup> and iodine forms I<sup>−</sup>; the charges must add to zero.

items.q: What is the octet rule?
c: Atoms tend to gain, lose or share electrons to have 8 in their outer shell.

items.q: What is the formula of calcium fluoride?

items.q: Sr<sup>2+</sup> and N<sup>3−</sup> ions combine. What is the formula of the compound?
items.e: Use the lowest numbers that make the total charge zero: 3 × (+2) + 2 × (−3) = 0.

items.q: What happens in an ionic bond?
